To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oral administration of 50 mg of 5-FUI emulsion per day for 2 weeks prior to gastrectomy for cancer of the stomach resulted in a 62% reduction in the number of patients with lymph node metastases and in a 60% reduction in the size of metastatic lesions in the lymph nodes, as compared with the number of patients and size of lesions in a control group that did not receive the 5-FUI.

oral administration of 50–100 mg of a 5-FU fat emulsion per kg of body weight, 2–3 hours before surgery, is effective in increasing the concentration of 50-FU in the lymph nodes, and in inducing necrosis or degeneration of metastases in the lymph nodes.
the oral 5-Fu emulsion is absorbed mainly through the lymphatic system, and is effective as an ad juvant to the surgical therapy of gastric cancer.

the development of an adjuvant therapy using a 5-FU fat emulsion, administered orally, in patients with gastric cancer, particularly those with lymph node metastases.

oral administration of an emulsified 5-FU solution, as an adjuv ant to surgery, was effective in the treatment of patients with gastric cancer, especially those with lymph node metastases, and that this method is a simple and safe way to administer the drug.

it is not the size of a tumor that determines whether a patient is likely to survive, but rather the location of the tumor.
